notes.text: Nikolaj Ehlers is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Taylor Hall has taken his spot beside Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Pavel Dorofeyev is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. Will Cuylle has taken his spot beside J.T. Miller and Tye Kartye.
Gabe Perreault is out 4-6 weeks (lower body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Taylor Raddysh has taken his spot beside Mika Zibanejad and Alexis Lafrenière.
Max Sasson joined from VAN on Nov 21 and has played beside Glenn Gawdin and Matt Rempe.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 34% of the team’s shorthanded time in 17 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

stakes: The Rangers go in fourth in the Metropolitan with 27 points, 14 points behind the Hurricanes, first.

story.head: Unstoppable force vs. immovable object
paras: The Hurricanes already played in New York once this season and left with a 5-2 win on Nov 22. The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak, while the Hurricanes have won three straight. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Canes first (second in the NHL) and the Rangers fourth (18th).

The Hurricanes’ record (.820) is about what their chances are worth. The Rangers have played better than their record (.540) says: their chances are worth about .612, and their finishing has held them back.

The Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st). The Rangers, by contrast, let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd). The Hurricanes also give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd), so the Rangers could find some good looks against them. Carolina has scored 4.12 goals a game, the most in the league, and allowed 2.20, the fewest. As for the Rangers, they get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd) and hit a lot (2nd). The Rangers’ power play against the Hurricanes’ penalty killers is strength against strength.

Sebastian Aho (13 G / 21 A / 34 P in 25 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, and Logan Stankoven (11 G / 13 A / 24 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (2 G / 26 A / 28 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Alexis Lafrenière (10 G / 12 A / 22 P in 25 GP) has a team-high ten goals.

Dylan Garand (7-9-1 / .907 SV% in 15 GS) will likely start for the Rangers. Carolina has two options in net: Pyotr Kochetkov (13-1-1 / .910 SV% in 15 GS) and Brandon Bussi (6-2-2 / .891 SV% in 10 GS). Kochetkov has started six of their last ten games, but Bussi got the last one on Wednesday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
The Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Rangers do.
